definition: Early warning and public alerting detect an impending hazard or communicate timely warnings to exposed people, institutions or responders so that protective action can be taken. Counts when the project finances, develops, procures, deploys or explicitly requires warning-generation systems, alert dissemination platforms, cell broadcast, emergency messaging or other dedicated public-warning capabilities. The defining function is warning or alerting: production of climate or hydrometeorological information without an alert function belongs to climate_information_systems, while warnings and protective instructions before or during the hazard count, and coordination, damage reporting and response after it do not. A system performing both information and warning functions may receive both labels when the functions are separately explicit. Does not count for routine communications, call centers, general emergency response, post-disaster connectivity, existing warning systems mentioned only as context or lessons from previous disasters. Alerts about events that are not hazards (traffic, service interruptions, appointment or payment reminders), reporting damage or incidents after the event, and a claim that new connectivity or digital services will help warnings reach people do not count. Hazard alerts to road users count; traffic alerts do not.
boundary: The project warns or alerts people or institutions about an imminent hazard.
note: Keep post-disaster communications outside this measure.
